A scribes lecturn fills the eastern side of the room, in and around it are pages Marley's "great novel"… which so far is mostly derivative and scattered rehashes of other writer's work.

In the southwest corner are two display cases which contains books that Morlibint deems to be too valuable or sensitive to leave in the public room. He normally carries the key.

A sumptuous bed with feather comforters and pillows occupies much of this room. A book shelf in the south west seems strangely mixed in no particular order. You find a fanciful tale of a fey prince, beside a text describing mechanical principles in clockwork.

Dressers to either side contain the personal effects of the residents. On one side of the room is an easel and a haphazard stack of paintings. All of them quite lovely, mostly portraiture of workmen, common folk and daily life they are signed with a simple 'C'

This cozy bookshop is orderly and clean. (Unseen servants do most of the work!) The shelves are packed with stories of adventure, mystery and magic - with smaller sections for non-fiction and academia. A few chairs are placed here and there in the room, allowing customers to browse and read comfortably.


A red velvet curtain is drawn to the north, beneath a small sign marked 'Private', behind a desk near the back of a shop is a locked door labeled 'special collections'

This well appointed kitchen, is filled with delightful odors and food in various stages of preparation or consumption. A large wood fired oven sits on the south wall, with a table for four set in the middle of the room. Marley is a gifted cook, an usually has some food laid out on the table or shelves.

This well stocked pantry has plenty of fresh food, preserves and supplies. Enough to last the pair for months if needed. Carlisle is a bit of a 'Prepper' - and has ensured that they have everything they need in case of emergency or famine.

The smell of fresh ink and paper fills this chamber, in the center of the room stand an old printing press. Painstakingly brought here from the captial at considerable expense. Crates of supplies, tools and projects line the walls to the north.

A simple trap door that can be bolted from this side leads back down to the main floor. On the west wall a large window lets in natural light and provides a view of the street outfront. At the back room a large sliding door provides cargo access to the attic. A large winch is bolted to the floor a few feet away from the door and spools of rope lay in the corner.

A hammock hangs in one corner. This room is Carlisle's sanctuary and workshop in one.

Marley and Carlisle rarely entertain. This rooms seems to have been furnished more to provide them with a place to lounge in comfort. With a comfy sofa on one wall, and a more firm chaise-lounge on the other. A mirrored vanity desk sits against one wall with drawers containing simple grooming supplies.


A valuable antique clockwork grandfather clock tone sonorously on the hour.
Light streams into this room from large glass windows, illuminating a small table where Marley enjoys a spot of tea with Carlisle or favoured guests. He can often be found sitting here reading.

Marley

Marley is a friendly shopkeeper and armchair adventurer who has a passion for fantastic tales of mystery and magic. He is generally warm and outgoing. He loves to inspire the minds and imaginations of people, "the true source of magic" as he will often say. He stammers a little in conversation, but is quick witted and a little sarcastic. (Bob Newhart is my real world inspiration for roleplaying him)

Marley would rather enjoy a cup of team and read about adventure rather than risk his own health and comfort. "Everything there is to learn you can read in a book." He has a scattered collection of fan-fic quality half-finished stories which he is certain will someday be a great work of fiction.

He is extremely well read, and curious about any any all subjects arcane and occult. Though he can be a bit squeamish with the details. He enjoys creature comforts and luxury more than most, and is a little bit greedy. Not selfishly so, but he will often "upsell" customers or provide them with more than they really needed at additional expense.

Carlisle

Carlisle is a pragmatic and active person who is deeply engaged in the community and local politics. He operates the only printing press in the area from the attic above the bookshop and uses it to publish mostly non-fiction, textbooks for the school, and socialist political pamphlets. It was he who arranged the lucrative contract with a local noble giving the shop a steady source of income. Though he is uncomfortable with working for the "Bourgeoisie" both the bookshop and the press need money - he is foremost a practical man.

Nevertheless he does publish and distribute posters and pamphlets that promote safe working conditions in the mills and forestry industry, and expose the excesses of the lumber barons and the upper class. He is well liked among the workers, who may not always understand what he's on about, but appreciate that he's on their side. On the other hand, the Mayor and many others often do not appreciate what is being written.

A Couple

Marley and Carlisle met at University in the capital. Students of literature and the power of the written word, each applies and interprets its application differently. Many spirited philosophical debates brought them closer together and they have a deep respect and love for each other. Marley reaching for people's hearts and minds, and Carlisle for their health and wellbeing. But rather than conflicting they came to see it as two sides of the same coin - though even today they have heated discussions at the table!

When Carlisle activism made staying in the capital difficult, they decided to move to a small town. Back to the basics, to the people, where they could be a beacon of learning and education. The bookshop was established….

A simply furnished and magically maintained water closet. The floor is covered with a wicker mat, so it's not so cold on the feet when you get out of the tub. The cabinet on the north wall contains clean towels, soaps and other toiletries.

This top of the tower provides panoramic views of the village from the many large windows that circle the room. The floor is graven with an image aligned to the cardinal directions, and both a magical astrolabe and powerful telescope sit here mostly unused.


It is a rather sparsely appointed workroom for a wizard really. Marley spends more time here working on his "great novel" rather than practicing magic or researching rituals. His spell book sit on a bookstand to the east, and several valuable scrolls and useful texts are scattered about. As are the contents of an alchemy kit and a few unfinished projects.
